#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
#two classes for these two environments
#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
class race_environment:
    '''A class to manage the race'''
    
    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def __init__(self, config):
        '''Set up the constructor
            Takes -- config, a dictionary specifying the track dimensions and initial state
        '''
        self.track = np.zeros((config['track_shape']['height']
                  ,config['track_shape']['width']))    #set up an array to represent the track
        self.track[config['track_shape']['v_track_width']:,config['track_shape']['h_track_width']:] = 1    #block the no-go area
        self.state = {}
        if not config['starting_position']:
            self.state['position'] = {'X':np.random.choice(a = range(config['track_shape']['v_track_width']))
                                      ,'Y':config['track_shape']['height']-1}
        else:
            self.state['position'] = copy.deepcopy(config['starting_position'])
        if not config['starting_velocity']:
            self.state['V'] = {'V':0,'H':0}
        else:
            self.state['V'] = copy.deepcopy(config['starting_velocity'])    #set up the state -- here it will be position and velocity
        self.old_position = copy.deepcopy(self.state['position'])
        self.config = config        
        
    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def reset(self):
        '''A function to reset to initial conditions'''
        self.state = {'position':{'X':np.random.choice(a = range(self.config['track_shape']['v_track_width']))
                                      ,'Y':self.config['track_shape']['height']-1}
                      ,'V':{'V':0,'H':0}}    #set up the state -- here it will be position and velocity
        self.old_position = copy.deepcopy(self.state['position'])

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@    
    def update_V(self,a):
        '''A function to update vert and horiz velocity
            Takes -- a, a dictionary containing the vert and horiz acceleration
        '''
        self.state['V']['V'] = min(5,max(0,self.state['V']['V'] + a['V']))    #update the vert velocity
        self.state['V']['H'] = min(5,self.state['V']['H'] + a['H'])    #update the horiz velocity

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@    
    def update_Position(self):
        '''A function to update vert and horiz position
        '''        
        self.state['position']['X'] = self.state['position']['X'] + self.state['V']['H']    #update the horiz position
        self.state['position']['Y'] = self.state['position']['Y'] - self.state['V']['V']    #update the vert position

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@    
    def obstacle_check(self):
        '''A function to check if the player crosses an obstacle'''
        crash = False
        if self.state['position']['X'] != self.old_position['X']:
            m = (self.state['position']['Y'] - self.old_position['Y'])/(self.state['position']['X'] - self.old_position['X'])
            b = self.state['position']['Y'] - m*self.state['position']['X']
            xs = np.linspace(start = self.old_position['X']
                        ,stop = self.state['position']['X']
                        ,num = 2*abs(self.state['position']['X'] - self.old_position['X']) + 1)
            ys = np.round(m*xs + b)
            xs = np.round(xs)
            for x,y in zip(xs,ys):

                if self.track[int(y),int(x)] == 1:
                    crash = True
                    break
        else:
            if self.track[self.state['position']['Y'],self.state['position']['X']] == 1:    #and if the agent is in the no-go
                crash = True    #set crash to true
        return crash

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@    
    def check_crash(self):
        '''A function to check if the agent crashed'''
        crash = False
        if self.state['position']['X'] < 0:    #if the agent goes out of bounds to the left
            crash = True    #set crash to true
        if self.state['position']['Y'] < 0:    #if the agent goes out of bounds to the top
            crash = True    #set crash to true
        if self.state['position']['X'] >= 0 and self.state['position']['X'] < self.config['track_shape']['width']-1 and self.state['position']['Y'] >= 0:    #if the agent is within the array
            crash = self.obstacle_check()
        return crash

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def check_win(self):
        '''A function to check if the agent won'''
        win = False    #assume no win
        if self.state['position']['X'] >= self.config['track_shape']['width'] and self.state['position']['Y'] < self.config['track_shape']['h_track_width']:    #if the agent is over the finish line
            win = True    #set win to true
        return win

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def reward(self,sp):
        return 1/max(1,((sp['X'] - (self.config['track_shape']['width'] - 1))**2
                          + (self.config['track_shape']['h_track_width']/2.0 - sp['Y'])**2))
        
    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def step(self,a):
        '''A function to evolve the environment
            Takes -- a, a dictionary containing the vert and horiz acceleration
        '''
        outcome = ''    #track crash/win
        done = False    #set the done indicator
        self.update_V(a)    #update the velocity
        self.update_Position()    #update the position
        crash = self.check_crash()    #check if the agent crashed
        self.old_position = copy.deepcopy(self.state['position'])
        r = self.reward(self.state['position'])
        if crash:
            outcome = 'crash'
        if not crash:    #if the agent didn't crash...
            win = self.check_win()    #check if the agent won
            if win:
                outcome = 'won'
                done = True
                r = 10
        return {'state':self.state
                     ,'reward':r
                     ,'done':done
                    ,'Win/Lost':outcome}

Modifying the environment (section 2)¶

In the original class a crash just gets flagged and the car keeps going from wherever it ended up. The lab wants a crash to send the car back to a random cell on the start line with velocity 0, and the episode keeps going. I did that with a small subclass so the example class stays the same. Its reset() already does exactly that (random start cell, both speeds 0).

In [5]:
class modified_race_environment(race_environment):
    '''Same race, but a crash sends the car back to the start line and the episode keeps going'''

    def step(self, a):
        out = race_environment.step(self, a)
        if out['Win/Lost'] == 'crash':
            self.reset()    #random cell on the start line, velocity back to 0
            out['state'] = self.state
        return out

                              ,'h_track_width':h_track_width}
          ,'starting_position':None
         ,'starting_velocity':None}    #set up the config for the environment

In [7]:
agent_config['alpha'] = 0.5    #step size for SARSA and expected SARSA (MC just averages returns)
agent_config['Q0'] = 0.0    #starting Q-value for every state-action pair

MAX_STEPS = 1000    #an episode that hasn't finished by now gets cut off and counts as a fail
N_EPISODES = 3000    #training episodes per run

def to_dict(a):
    '''actions are (vertical change, horizontal change) tuples, the env wants a dict'''
    return {'V': a[0], 'H': a[1]}

Random races (section 3.2)¶

100 races picking one of the 9 actions uniformly at random every turn. I ran it on the modified track and on the original one, where I count a crash as the end of the race like in lab 2. Random races on the modified track don't need a step cap since they always finish eventually.

In [8]:
def random_races(env, n_races=100, crash_ends_race=False):
    turns, won = [], []
    for i in range(n_races):
        env.reset()
        n = 0
        while True:
            a = agent_config['A'][np.random.randint(len(agent_config['A']))]
            out = env.step(to_dict(a))
            n += 1
            if out['done'] or (crash_ends_race and out['Win/Lost'] == 'crash'):
                break
        turns.append(n)
        won.append(out['Win/Lost'] == 'won')
    return pd.DataFrame({'race': range(n_races), 'turns': turns, 'won': won})

np.random.seed(0)
random_modified = random_races(modified_race_environment(env_config))
random_original = random_races(renv, crash_ends_race=True)

random_modified.assign(track='modified').to_csv("results/random_races_modified.csv", index=False)
random_original.assign(track='original').to_csv("results/random_races_original.csv", index=False)

print("modified track: average turns to finish =", random_modified['turns'].mean(),
      "| median =", random_modified['turns'].median(), "| max =", random_modified['turns'].max())
print("original track (crash ends it): finished", random_original['won'].sum(), "of 100 races,",
      "average race length =", random_original['turns'].mean())

State and rewards (sections 4.1 and 4.2)¶

State: (x, y, vertical speed, horizontal speed). Position alone isn't enough because the same cell at different speeds leads to different next cells. The track never changes so it doesn't need to be in the state. I store it as a tuple so it can be a dict key.

Reward 1 (example): the env already computes it. It's 1 / max(1, squared distance to the middle of the finish line) each turn, and 10 for crossing the finish line.

Reward 2 (mine): -1 every turn. The return is just minus the number of turns, so the best policy is the fastest race. Crashing isn't punished directly, but it sends you back to the start which costs a lot of turns.

In [9]:
def get_state(env_state):
    return (env_state['position']['X'], env_state['position']['Y'], env_state['V']['V'], env_state['V']['H'])

def reward_1(out):
    return out['reward']    #example reward, computed inside step()

def reward_2(out):
    return -1    #my reward, every turn costs 1

rewards = {'reward 1': reward_1, 'reward 2': reward_2}

Agent (section 4.3)¶

This fills in the example agent skeleton. Q is a dict that maps a state to an array of 9 action values, so I don't have to preallocate anything and every state starts at Q0. pi is epsilon-greedy, which counts as epsilon-soft since every action has at least epsilon/9 chance. update_Q is first visit MC, and I added one update for SARSA and one for expected SARSA.

In [10]:
class agent:
    '''A class to manage the agent'''

    def __init__(self, config):
        self.config = config
        n_actions = len(config['A'])
        self.Q = defaultdict(lambda: np.full(n_actions, config['Q0']))
        self.N = defaultdict(lambda: np.zeros(n_actions))    #visit counts, only MC uses these

    def pi(self, state, epsilon):
        '''epsilon-greedy, ties between best actions are broken randomly'''
        if np.random.rand() < epsilon:
            return np.random.randint(len(self.config['A']))
        q = self.Q[state]
        return np.random.choice(np.flatnonzero(q == q.max()))

    def update_Q(self, trajectory):
        '''first visit MC, trajectory is the whole episode as a list of (s, a, r)'''
        gamma = self.config['gamma']
        first_visit = {}
        for t, (s, a, r) in enumerate(trajectory):
            if (s, a) not in first_visit:
                first_visit[(s, a)] = t
        G = 0
        for t in reversed(range(len(trajectory))):
            s, a, r = trajectory[t]
            G = gamma * G + r
            if first_visit[(s, a)] == t:
                self.N[s][a] += 1
                self.Q[s][a] += (G - self.Q[s][a]) / self.N[s][a]    #running average of the returns

    def update_sarsa(self, s, a, r, s2, a2, done):
        target = r if done else r + self.config['gamma'] * self.Q[s2][a2]
        self.Q[s][a] += self.config['alpha'] * (target - self.Q[s][a])

    def update_expected_sarsa(self, s, a, r, s2, done):
        #average of Q(s2, .) under epsilon-greedy instead of the one action we sampled
        eps = self.config['epsilon']
        q = self.Q[s2]
        expected = (1 - eps) * q.max() + eps * q.mean()
        target = r if done else r + self.config['gamma'] * expected
        self.Q[s][a] += self.config['alpha'] * (target - self.Q[s][a])

Training loop¶

Every run resets the seed to 0 so runs are comparable. For each episode I record the length, the return (plain sum of rewards, not discounted), and whether it crossed the finish line before MAX_STEPS.

greedy_test runs 100 races with epsilon = 0 after training, so I can see what the learned policy does without the exploration noise.

In [11]:
def train(method, reward_fn, config):
    np.random.seed(0)
    env = modified_race_environment(env_config)
    ag = agent(config)
    eps = config['epsilon']
    rows = []
    for ep in tqdm(range(N_EPISODES), desc=method):
        env.reset()
        s = get_state(env.state)
        a = ag.pi(s, eps)
        trajectory = []
        G = 0
        for t in range(MAX_STEPS):
            out = env.step(to_dict(config['A'][a]))
            r = reward_fn(out)
            s2 = get_state(out['state'])
            G += r
            a2 = ag.pi(s2, eps)
            if method == 'MC':
                trajectory.append((s, a, r))
            elif method == 'SARSA':
                ag.update_sarsa(s, a, r, s2, a2, out['done'])
            else:
                ag.update_expected_sarsa(s, a, r, s2, out['done'])
            s, a = s2, a2
            if out['done']:
                break
        if method == 'MC':
            ag.update_Q(trajectory)    #MC only learns once the episode is over
        rows.append({'episode': ep, 'length': t + 1, 'return': G, 'success': int(out['done'])})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), ag

def greedy_test(ag, n_races=100):
    env = modified_race_environment(env_config)
    lengths, wins = [], []
    for i in range(n_races):
        env.reset()
        s = get_state(env.state)
        for t in range(MAX_STEPS):
            out = env.step(to_dict(ag.config['A'][ag.pi(s, 0.0)]))
            s = get_state(out['state'])
            if out['done']:
                break
        lengths.append(t + 1)
        wins.append(out['done'])
    return np.mean(lengths), np.mean(wins)

def summarize(df, ag):
    greedy_len, greedy_win = greedy_test(ag)
    return {'episodes': len(df),
            'total steps': df['length'].sum(),
            'length first 100': df['length'][:100].mean(),
            'length last 100': df['length'][-100:].mean(),
            'success first 100': df['success'][:100].mean(),
            'success last 100': df['success'][-100:].mean(),
            'greedy length': greedy_len,
            'greedy success': greedy_win}

def plot_curves(run_dfs, title, filename):
    '''run_dfs maps a label to a training dataframe, curves are 100 episode moving averages'''
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4))
    for label, df in run_dfs.items():
        smooth = df.rolling(100, min_periods=1).mean()
        axes[0].plot(df['episode'], smooth['length'], label=label)
        axes[1].plot(df['episode'], smooth['return'], label=label)
        axes[2].plot(df['episode'], smooth['success'], label=label)
    axes[0].set_yscale('log')
    for ax, name in zip(axes, ['episode length', 'return', 'success rate']):
        ax.set_title(title + ': ' + name)
        ax.set_xlabel('episode')
        ax.set_ylabel(name + ' (100 episode avg)')
    axes[0].legend()
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("figures/" + filename, dpi=150)
    plt.show()

Summary table¶
total steps is how many turns of experience each run used in total, which is a fair way to compare sample
efficiency since an early episode can be 1000 turns and a late one 20.


















In [14]:






summary = pd.DataFrame([dict(method=m, reward=rname, **summarize(df, ag)) for (m, rname), (df, ag) in runs.items()])
summary.to_csv("results/training_summary.csv", index=False)
summary.round(2)

Initial vs learned Q-values (Q5)¶
Every Q-value starts at 0. Below is what they look like after training. "Start line max Q" is the best action
value from the 10 start states (velocity 0), averaged over the 10 cells. For reward 2 a perfect estimate of a race
that takes T turns would be -(1 - 0.9^T) / 0.1, which is close to -10 for anything longer than about 20 turns.


















In [15]:






q_rows = []
for (m, rname), (df, ag) in runs.items():
    best_q = np.array([q.max() for q in ag.Q.values()])
    n_states = len(ag.Q)
    start_q = np.mean([ag.Q[(x, height - 1, 0, 0)].max() for x in range(v_track_width)])
    q_rows.append({'method': m, 'reward': rname, 'states seen': n_states, 'initial Q': agent_config['Q0'],
                   'start line max Q': start_q, 'mean max Q': best_q.mean(),
                   'min max Q': best_q.min(), 'largest Q': best_q.max()})
q_table = pd.DataFrame(q_rows)
q_table.to_csv("results/q_values.csv", index=False)
q_table.round(3)

What the agent does on the track (Q4)¶
Most (cell, velocity) pairs never get visited, so showing the greedy action for a made up velocity would mostly
show untrained zeros. Instead I start a greedy (epsilon = 0) race from each of the 10 start cells and draw the
path plus an arrow at each turn for the action picked (which way it pushes the velocity). A black dot means it
kept the velocity the same. I compare MC and SARSA, both trained on the example reward.


















In [16]:






def plot_policy(ag, ax, title):
    ax.imshow(renv.track, cmap='Greys', vmin=0, vmax=2)    #gray = off the track
    for x0 in range(v_track_width):
        env = modified_race_environment(dict(env_config, starting_position={'X': x0, 'Y': height - 1}))
        xs, ys, push_h, push_v = [], [], [], []
        for t in range(100):
            pos = env.state['position']
            a = ag.config['A'][ag.pi(get_state(env.state), 0.0)]
            xs.append(pos['X'])
            ys.append(pos['Y'])
            push_v.append(a[0])
            push_h.append(a[1])
            out = env.step(to_dict(a))
            if out['done'] or out['Win/Lost'] == 'crash':
                break
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color='tab:blue', alpha=0.5)
        ax.quiver(xs, ys, push_h, push_v, color='tab:red', scale=25, width=0.006)    #positive V push points up
        still = [i for i in range(len(xs)) if push_h[i] == 0 and push_v[i] == 0]
        ax.scatter([xs[i] for i in still], [ys[i] for i in still], color='black', s=8)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel('x (cell)')
    ax.set_ylabel('y (cell, 0 = top)')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 7))
plot_policy(runs[('MC', 'reward 1')][1], axes[0], 'MC, reward 1: greedy paths and actions')
plot_policy(runs[('SARSA', 'reward 1')][1], axes[1], 'SARSA, reward 1: greedy paths and actions')
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/policy_mc_vs_sarsa.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
















































Effect of gamma and epsilon (Q6)¶
SARSA on the example reward, changing one thing at a time from the base (gamma = 0.9, epsilon = 0.1).


















In [17]:






ge_runs = {'gamma 0.9, eps 0.1 (base)': runs[('SARSA', 'reward 1')]}
for g in [0.5, 0.99]:
    ge_runs['gamma ' + str(g)] = train('SARSA', reward_1, dict(agent_config, gamma=g))
for e in [0.01, 0.3]:
    ge_runs['eps ' + str(e)] = train('SARSA', reward_1, dict(agent_config, epsilon=e))

pd.concat([df.assign(run=label) for label, (df, ag) in ge_runs.items()]).to_csv(
    "results/gamma_epsilon_curves.csv", index=False)
ge_summary = pd.DataFrame([dict(run=label, **summarize(df, ag)) for label, (df, ag) in ge_runs.items()])
ge_summary.to_csv("results/gamma_epsilon_summary.csv", index=False)
ge_summary.round(2)

plot_curves({k: ge_runs[k][0] for k in ['gamma 0.9, eps 0.1 (base)', 'gamma 0.5', 'gamma 0.99']},
            'SARSA, gamma', "gamma_sarsa.png")

            'SARSA, epsilon', "epsilon_sarsa.png")



























































Wrecking the learning (section 5)¶
Failure 1, no exploration (epsilon = 0), example reward. Every Q starts at 0 and reward 1 is always
positive, so whatever action the agent tries first gets a positive value and beats all the untried 0s. With no
epsilon it never tries anything else, so I expect it to lock onto whatever it did first and never find the
finish.


Failure 2, bad reward: +1 for every turn. Now the return is bigger the longer the race lasts, so the best
thing to do is never cross the finish line. Crashing doesn't hurt either since it just restarts the car. I
expect episodes to run all the way to MAX_STEPS.

Repairing failure 1 without turning epsilon back on¶
Keep epsilon = 0 but start every Q-value at 20 instead of 0. That's way above any return the agent can actually
get with reward 1 (about 10), so every action it hasn't tried yet looks better than the ones it has. Each time it
tries one the value drops toward the real return, so a greedy agent ends up trying everything. The exploration
comes from optimism instead of randomness.


















In [20]:






optimistic = dict(agent_config, epsilon=0.0, Q0=20.0)
for m in methods:
    wreck_runs[(m, 'no exploration + Q0 = 20')] = train(m, reward_1, optimistic)

pd.concat([df.assign(method=m, case=case) for (m, case), (df, ag) in wreck_runs.items()]).to_csv(
    "results/wreck_curves.csv", index=False)
